title: IS12:: factorial.c (4.4)

lines.code: Primary objective: practicing simple while loop with countdown control
Secondary objective: printing values of iterative functions

lines.explanation: We need to use input/output library since we are using printf and scanf in this program.

lines.code: int n = 1; /* this number will run from 1 to n in the loop */
lines.explanation: This variable called "running variable" - it changes with each iteration of the loop running from 1 to n

lines.code: long old_factorial = 1; /* the previous value of factorial for n-1 */
lines.explanation: This variable will hold q value of the factorial. Since it can be pretty large, we use long instead of int

lines.code: long new_factorial; /* the value of factorial(n) to be calculated */
lines.explanation: This variable will hold q value of the factorial. Since it can be pretty large, we use long instead of int
This line simply prints a nice header for our program (with an extra new line skipped).

The value entered by the user is nothing else but the number of times to run the loop. We know that by assigning it to the loop control variable in a countdown loop we can make the loop running exactly the specified number of times.

At each iteration of the loop, the current value of the counter is checked. If this value is zero (0), the loop will will be skipped, otherwise loop statements will be executed. After the value of counter is used for checking, it is decremented (post-decr
This statement calculates the new value of factorial using current value of n and the previous value of the factorial.
The new value of factorial - factorial(n) - is printed in a "nice way". Note that we use %ld specification instead of %d since we need to print value of type long.
The running variable is incremented to prepare for the next step of the loop.
For the next statement of the loop the current new value will be the "old" (previous) value. Here we are preparing for it.
This statement ends the block that serves as the loop body
This is the end of the program. Note that that the loop statement ends the program - there is no statement after the loop. This is normal.
